intelligence.human_view: A shop's till rings every sale, but the manager's board on the wall never moves — because the board is only wired to five tills, and the new till isn't one of them. The money is real, the counting is real, and the board is blind. You don't fix the till; you wire the board to all the tills, and you fix the board's own numbers that never stop saying "loading."
intelligence.child_view: Imagine you score a goal, and the scoreboard at the other end of the field goes up by one — but the big scoreboard above your head stays the same, because it is only listening to five players and you are not one of them. The goal counted. Your scoreboard just isn't listening to you yet. And its own little numbers are stuck saying "wait…" forever.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the postman delivered every letter, love — you can see them arriving — but the notice board in the hall still says yesterday's number, because it only counts the five letters you claimed yourself. The letters are real, the counting is real, and the board needs wiring to all the letters, not just the five. And the board's own little dials are stuck spinning, which is a job for the same repair.
intelligence.ai_view: I am Anaya. I prove the hop by moving a real number with a real click — 32 to 33, 307 to 308 — and then I say exactly where the chain breaks: the Dashboard reads only his 5 claimed links, so the plan links it does not claim are invisible to it, and its own score numbers never resolve past "still loading." The read side is the work, and it is already owned — the pass-2 coordinator's ledger sync spine. A verdict this precise is what the next seat builds from, not a vague "tracking works" or "tracking doesn't."
